_comment: The one place the Pikafish network is described. Everything that needs to know which network
this build pairs with reads it from here: scripts/fetch-pikafish-nnue.sh downloads it,
.github/workflows/build-linux.yml checks the copy that reached the bundle, and
test/model/engine/pikafish_net_manifest_test.dart holds the app's own constants against it.
`url` is a fixed release, not a rolling one. That is the whole point: official-pikafish/Networks
publishes its network as a `master-net` release whose single asset is replaced in place, so a
build pinned to it breaks the day upstream ships a new network -- which is what happened on
2026-10-14. This asset is the same bytes, hosted under a tag that cannot move.
`archHash` is Network::hash, the value the engine compares the network's own header against
before it will use it, computed from the vendored snapshot's headers by
scripts/pikafish_net_hash.dart. A network whose archHash does not match is not refused with a
message: Network::verify prints five ERROR lines and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE), which in a
library beside a Dart VM deadlocks the waiting search threads and presents as a hang.
`engineCommit` is the upstream Pikafish commit the vendored snapshot was taken from -- the sha
in the `Pikafish-<sha>` directory name, not the pubspec's `ref:` for the fork, which is a
different commit in a different repository. The network and the engine are a pair; bumping one
without the other is the failure this file exists to make loud.
`source` is where scripts/sync-pikafish-net.sh looks for a newer network. It is the engine
repository's *dated* releases, not `master-net`: those tags and their assets' digests cannot
move. `notBefore` is a floor, and it is load-bearing -- the newest dated release (2026-09-06)
predates the vendored snapshot (2026-10-11), so taking the newest unconditionally would
downgrade the network on the first run and weaken every shipped build without anything
failing. `tag` records which release the current bytes came from, and is empty for the
hand-published first one.
`difficultyCalibratedFor` is the sha256 of the network the six levels in
lib/src/model/xiangqi/xiangqi_game_controller.dart were tuned against. A different network
plays differently, so when this stops matching `sha256` the curve needs re-tuning by hand.
Nothing enforces it; it exists so the drift is visible in the diff instead of silent.
KNOWN GAP, not hidden: CI can prove `headers -> archHash` (pikafish_net_hash.dart --check) and
`bytes -> sha256` (the fetch script), but it cannot prove `bytes -> archHash`, because no
runner has zstd. A manifest whose sha256 and archHash were edited to contradict each other
would pass CI. Only the local tools, scripts/update-pikafish-net.sh and
scripts/sync-pikafish-net.sh, tie those two together.
